title: Owner setup: create AnthonyPluth/fleet, its rulesets, the fleet-bot GitHub App and the consumers' secrets
body:
Key `FLEET-SETUP`

**Context**
`AnthonyPluth/fleet` is the new public repository for what Waypoint, Runway and Darkroom share: reusable workflows, the shared Python tools, the shared `AGENTS.md` sections and a Claude Code plugin marketplace. A few steps need the owner's admin rights and can't be done by an agent. fleet is public, so nothing personal goes into it: no hostnames, household data, account ids or tokens.

**Scope**
1. Create the public repository `AnthonyPluth/fleet` with only a README. Pick the license and write it in a comment here: AGPL-3.0 (as Waypoint and Runway) or a permissive one (MIT/Apache-2.0) if others should be able to call the workflows without license questions. `FLEET-SCAFFOLD` uses the answer.
2. Ruleset on `main`: pull request required, Code Owner review required, required checks `fleet CI` and `Self-test` (both added by `FLEET-SCAFFOLD`; add them once they have run once), no force push, no deletion.
3. Tag ruleset on `refs/tags/v*`: creation only by the owner and GitHub Actions (the release workflow), no update, no deletion. Consumers pin a commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment and the reusable workflows fetch their own scripts by tag, so a tag must never move. Turn on immutable releases if the setting is offered.
4. Security settings: private vulnerability reporting, Dependabot alerts and security updates, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL default setup (Python and GitHub Actions).
5. fleet's own secret for dogfooding the review on fleet's pull requests: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (as Waypoint and Runway).
6. GitHub App `fleet-bot` (private, owned by AnthonyPluth, no webhook). Repository permissions: Contents read and write, Pull requests read and write, Metadata read. No Workflows permission, so a token from it can never change a file under `.github/workflows/`. Install it on Waypoint, Runway and Darkroom only (not on fleet). In each of the three repos add the variable `FLEET_BOT_APP_ID` and the secret `FLEET_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY`; nothing of the App goes into fleet.
7. Labels in fleet: `manual`, `security`, `safety-critical`, `workflows`, `plugin`, `tools`, `release`, `review-mining`. In the app repos: see this backlog's README ("New labels").

**Out of scope**
Any file beyond the README (`FLEET-SCAFFOLD` and later).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `AnthonyPluth/fleet` exists, public, license choice recorded here.
- [ ] Both rulesets exist (screenshot or settings export pasted here, no secrets).
- [ ] `fleet-bot` installed on exactly Waypoint, Runway and Darkroom with the permissions above; `FLEET_BOT_APP_ID` and `FLEET_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` set in each.
- [ ] Labels created.

**Tests**
None (settings).

**Depends on**
Nothing.

**Model**
Owner (no coding model).

title: Scaffold: package layout, Makefile, fleet's own CI and the FLEET_REF convention
body:
Key `FLEET-SCAFFOLD`

**Context**
fleet holds one copy of what Waypoint (`AnthonyPluth/Waypoint`) and Runway (`AnthonyPluth/Runway`) carry twice today, and what Darkroom would otherwise copy a third time: `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` + `.github/scripts/agent_review.py` + `.github/agent-review/`, `merge-gate.yml` + `.github/scripts/merge-gate.sh`, `security.yml`, `tools/fleet_checks.py`, `tools/no_comments.py`, `tools/coverage_floor.py`, `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` and the shared parts of `AGENTS.md`. Consumers use it by pinned reference only. Where the two repos' conventions differ, fleet's own code follows the stricter one (Waypoint's): no comments or docstrings in Python, actions pinned by SHA with a version comment, bash `-eo pipefail` as each workflow's default shell, `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout.

A called (reusable) workflow can't reliably learn its own ref: `github.workflow_ref` and `github.workflow_sha` describe the caller. Each reusable workflow therefore carries the tag it belongs to and fetches its scripts, prompts and tools from fleet at that tag (the FLEET_REF convention below); the release stamps it (`FLEET-RELEASE`).

**Scope**
- Layout:

```text
fleet/
  VERSION  CHANGELOG.md  README.md  LICENSE  SECURITY.md  AGENTS.md  CLAUDE.md  Makefile  pyproject.toml
  fleet_tools/            cli.py config.py (reads [tool.fleet] from a consumer's pyproject.toml with tomllib) self_check.py
                          later: checks/ no_comments.py coverage_floor.py next_version.py test_timings.py agent_review.py
                                 review_mine.py sync.py drift.py screenshot_diff.py
  .github/workflows/      ci.yml ("fleet CI"), self-test.yml ("Self-test"); reusable workflows land beside them
  .github/agent-review/   (FLEET-REVIEW)    .github/scripts/ (FLEET-REVIEW, FLEET-MERGE-GATE)
  .claude-plugin/ plugins/fleet/            (FLEET-PLUGIN)
  agents-md/sections/                       (FLEET-AGENTS-MD)
  docs/                   adopting.md drift.md release.md (later issues fill them)
  tests/                  unittest suite; fixtures/consumer-waypoint/ and fixtures/consumer-runway/ (minimal trees with each app's layout and pyproject [tool.fleet]); fakes/
```

- `pyproject.toml`: package `fleet_tools`, `requires-python = ">=3.11"` and no runtime dependencies (stdlib only), so a runner's or a cloud container's system `python3` runs it without Poetry; console script `fleet = fleet_tools.cli:main`; Poetry dev group pinned: ruff, mypy (strict for `fleet_tools`), coverage, zizmor, actionlint (via its pinned binary download in CI).
- `fleet_tools/cli.py`: `fleet --version` (prints `VERSION`) and a subcommand registry the later issues add to.
- FLEET_REF convention: every reusable workflow (`on: workflow_call`) has a top-level `env: FLEET_REF: <tag>` and an optional input `fleet-ref`; its first step checks out `AnthonyPluth/fleet` at `inputs.fleet-ref || env.FLEET_REF` into `.fleet/` (sparse, `persist-credentials: false`). Until v1.0.0 the value is `main`. `fleet self-check` (fleet-only) fails when a reusable workflow lacks `FLEET_REF`, when its value differs from `v` + `VERSION` (or `main` while `VERSION` is 0.x), or when `self-test.yml` calls a reusable workflow without `fleet-ref: ${{ github.sha }}`.
- `Makefile`: `setup`, `check` (ruff, mypy, `python -m unittest discover tests`, `fleet self-check`, actionlint, zizmor over `.github/workflows/`), `fix`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ("fleet CI"): `make check` on every pull request and push to `main`. `.github/workflows/self-test.yml` ("Self-test"): on pull requests, calls each reusable workflow by local path (`uses: ./.github/workflows/<name>.yml`) with `fleet-ref: ${{ github.sha }}` and test inputs; it starts with one no-op job and each extraction issue adds its case.
- `VERSION` (`0.1.0`), `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog, with an Unreleased section), `README.md` (what fleet is, the pieces, a pointer to `docs/adopting.md`), `SECURITY.md` (private reporting; the trust model: fleet's workflows run inside the consumers with their secrets, so a change here is reviewed as a change to every consumer's own workflows), `LICENSE` (per `FLEET-SETUP`), `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`* @AnthonyPluth`), `.github/dependabot.yml` (github-actions and pip weekly with a 7-day cooldown, as the apps do), `.github/pull_request_template.md` (identical in both apps; copy it), `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` (the union of the two apps' templates: Scope, Acceptance criteria, Checks that will hold it, Depends on, Model), `.gitignore`.
- fleet's own `AGENTS.md` (later replaced in part by its own synced blocks, `FLEET-AGENTS-MD`) with the fleet rules: nothing personal in the repository, issues or PRs; every change is a change to three repositories' CI, so it bumps `CHANGELOG.md`'s Unreleased section; a change to an input, a status name or an AGENTS block is a breaking change unless it keeps the old behaviour by default. `CLAUDE.md`: Opus by default; Fable for anything touching the review workflows, secrets, untrusted pull request content or security scanning; Sonnet only for mechanical edits.

**Out of scope**
Every extraction (`FLEET-TOOLS` onward).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `make check` passes on a fresh clone; `fleet CI` and `Self-test` are green on the PR.
- [ ] `fleet self-check` fails on a fixture workflow without `FLEET_REF` and on one whose value disagrees with `VERSION` (tests).
- [ ] zizmor and actionlint report nothing on fleet's workflows.
- [ ] Nothing in the repository names a household member, a host, an account or a token (checked by the review on each PR).

**Tests**
`tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_self_check.py`, `tests/test_config.py` (`[tool.fleet]` parsing over the two fixture consumers).

**Depends on**
`FLEET-SETUP` (the repository exists).

**Model**
Opus: scaffold and CI with no secrets.

title: Extract the shared Python tools: fleet checks (union of both repos), no-comments, coverage floor, next version, test timings
body:
Key `FLEET-TOOLS`

**Context**
`tools/fleet_checks.py` differs between the two repos by about 400 lines; the core is the same and each repo grew checks the other lacks. Waypoint (443 lines): one Alembic head and a test per migration, the `Co-Authored-By` trailer, removed or skipped tests need a `Removes-Test:`/`Skips-Test:` trailer, workflow conventions (bash default, SHA pins with a version comment, paginated `gh api`, the `vars.RUNS_ON` pattern and a `# hosted:` comment on jobs that must stay on GitHub's runners), images only where they belong, skills well formed with `references/cli.md` current, the user feature map current, and mail parser fixtures (app-only). Runway (425 lines): the same core without the test-removal trailers, plus an `EARLY_ENV` rule (no step-only context in a job- or workflow-level `env`), images derived from pages and flows, a11y baseline shrink-only and flow inheritance (app-only). `tools/no_comments.py` and `tools/coverage_floor.py` exist only in Waypoint; `.github/scripts/next-version.sh` is identical in both; `tools/test_timings.py` differs by 25 lines.

**Scope**
- `fleet_tools/checks/`, split by concern, each the union of both versions: `migrations.py`, `commits.py` (model families `Opus|Sonnet|Haiku|Fable`, `Claude-Session`), `tests_removed.py` (Waypoint's trailers; Runway gains the check), `workflows.py` (both rule sets: Waypoint gains `EARLY_ENV`, Runway gains the `# hosted:` rule), `images.py` (homes, single files, a screenshot directory whose allowed names come from `verify.mjs`'s `PAGES` only (Waypoint) or pages and flows (Runway): config `names = "pages"` or `"pages-and-flows"`), `skills.py` (well formed; each configured generated reference equal to its generator's output; each configured generated feature map current).
- App-only checks stay in each app: `[tool.fleet] extra-checks = "tools.app_checks:CHECKS"` names a list of callables `fleet checks` imports from the consumer's tree and runs with the same reporting (Waypoint's mail parser fixtures; Runway's a11y baseline and flow inheritance move there in their adoption issues).
- Config: a `[tool.fleet]` table in the consumer's `pyproject.toml`. Example (Waypoint's values; the key names are settled in this PR and documented in `docs/adopting.md`):

```toml
[tool.fleet]
migrations = "waypoint/storage/migrations/versions"
migration-tests = "tests/test_migrations.py"
tested-from = "0001"
image-homes = ["docs/public/", "waypoint/static/", "waypoint/storage/logos/"]
image-files = ["docs/src/assets/logo.png"]
skills = ".claude/skills"
extra-checks = "tools.app_checks:CHECKS"

[tool.fleet.screenshots]
dir = "docs/src/assets/screenshots/"
names = "pages"
verify = "frontend/verify/verify.mjs"
flows = "frontend/verify/flows"

[[tool.fleet.generated]]
path = ".claude/skills/verify-waypoint/references/cli.md"
command = "make --no-print-directory -s verify-skill-print"

[tool.fleet.no-comments]
paths = ["waypoint", "tests", "tools", "frontend/src"]

[tool.fleet.coverage]
overall = 85
modules = { "waypoint/domain/" = 90, "waypoint/providers/" = 90, "waypoint/server/api/" = 90 }
```

- `fleet no-comments` (Waypoint's `tools/no_comments.py`, opt-in: runs only where `[tool.fleet.no-comments]` exists, so Runway's "match the surrounding comment density" convention is untouched), `fleet coverage-floor coverage.json` (Waypoint's, floors from config), `fleet next-version` (port of `next-version.sh`: PR title → semver bump, same outputs), `fleet test-timings` (union).
- `fleet checks [--commits BASE..HEAD]` is the one entry point `make fleet-checks` and CI call; output and exit codes as today's `tools/fleet_checks.py`.
- Port the tests: `tests/test_fleet_checks.py` from both repos, `tests/test_no_comments.py` and `tests/test_coverage_floor.py` from Waypoint, with app paths replaced by the fixture consumers.
- `docs/drift.md`: one row per drifted piece (this issue's and the later extractions'): what Waypoint does, what Runway does, what fleet takes, and why. Seed it with the rows in this backlog's README ("Drift resolved in fleet").

**Out of scope**
Reviews, merge gate, security workflow, AGENTS sync, the plugin.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every check from both repos' `tools/fleet_checks.py` exists in fleet, and the ported tests pass against `tests/fixtures/consumer-waypoint/` and `consumer-runway/`.
- [ ] Each check fires in each fixture consumer that configures it (a failing fixture per check) and is silent where it isn't configured.
- [ ] `extra-checks` loads a callable from the consumer tree and reports its findings in the same format; a missing module is a clear error, not a silent pass.
- [ ] `python3 -I -m fleet_tools.cli checks` runs on a runner's system Python with nothing installed (CI job).
- [ ] `docs/drift.md` covers every drifted file named in this issue.

**Tests**
`tests/test_checks_*.py` per module, `tests/test_no_comments.py`, `tests/test_coverage_floor.py`, `tests/test_next_version.py` (the shell script's cases), `tests/test_extra_checks.py`.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-SCAFFOLD`.

**Model**
Opus: a careful merge of two diverged tools; no secrets.

title: Reusable agent review (first review): agent-review.yml, agent_review.py, prompt, and findings that carry a kind
body:
Key `FLEET-REVIEW`

**Context**
Waypoint's and Runway's `agent-review.yml` share one design: `pull_request_target` runs main's copy; job `review` checks out main's prompt and scripts plus the pull request's code (to read only), runs Claude Code with Read, Grep and Glob confined to the review directory, no settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md, plugins or MCP servers (`.github/scripts/agent-review-run.sh`), and holds the secret; job `report` posts the comment and the "Agent review" status with a write token and never sees the code or the secrets. A re-review reads the diff since the last reviewed commit; a push that only merges main carries a passing verdict forward. That design must survive the extraction unchanged.

Drift: Waypoint's review is disabled (trigger commented out: "Codex reviews pull requests now"); Runway's runs, also on `ready_for_review`. Waypoint's `agent_review.py` never leaves fixtures, demo or sample data out of the diff (`SAMPLE_DATA`), knows more image types and has no docstrings; Runway's also leaves out `tests/fixtures/forecast_golden.json`. Both pin the model to Sonnet with no variable; Runway's header records the owner's decision that every review uses Sonnet.

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` with `on: workflow_call`:
  - inputs: `generated` (newline-separated paths left out of `diff.patch`), `first-review` (boolean, default `true`), `budget-usd` (default `3`) and `max-turns` (default `60`) (callers pass `${{ vars.AGENT_REVIEW_BUDGET_USD || '3' }}` and the like), `merge-gate-workflow` (default `merge-gate.yml`), `fleet-ref`, `dry-run` (self-test only: the report job prints instead of writing);
  - secrets, declared by name and optional: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (callers pass them by name; `secrets: inherit` isn't for cross-owner reuse and would hand over every secret);
  - jobs `review` and `report` as today, on `ubuntu-latest` with the `# hosted:` comment; the secrets appear only in the Review step's `env`.
- Trusted inputs: from fleet at FLEET_REF (sparse): `.github/agent-review/{prompt.md,incremental.md,schema.json,package.json,package-lock.json}`, `.github/scripts/agent-review-run.sh`, `fleet_tools/agent_review.py`; from the consumer's base commit (sparse): `AGENTS.md` and `.github/agent-review/context.md`. A consumer without `context.md` gets an `error` status that names the file.
- `prompt.md`: one generic prompt merged from both; the app description and what private data looks like there come from `context.md`; Waypoint's rule that fixtures, demo and sample data are always read and every changed image opened stays.
- `agent_review.py`: Waypoint's version (`SAMPLE_DATA`, the wider `IMAGES`, `USAGE` text, no docstrings) with `GENERATED` from the input; an explicit `generated` entry wins over `SAMPLE_DATA`, so Runway's golden fixture stays out. Runway's docstring explanations move to `docs/agent-review.md`.
- Triggers the caller declares: `pull_request_target` on `main` with `[opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, labeled, unlabeled]`. `ready_for_review` reviews only when the head has no "Agent review" status yet (a draft already reviewed isn't paid for twice); `labeled`/`unlabeled` don't rerun the first review (only `FLEET-SECOND-REVIEW` reacts to them). Concurrency is per job (`agent-review-<pr>`), so a label event can't cancel a running review.
- Findings gain a kind: `schema.json` adds required `kind` (the bold title of the AGENTS.md "Mistakes that keep coming back" item the finding falls under, verbatim, or `other`) and optional `check` (the lint, Semgrep rule, type or test that would have caught it). The comment keeps its marker on line 1 and state on line 2 and gains line 3, `<!-- agent-review-findings <base64 JSON> -->` (severity, kind, title, file per finding; titles defused; at most 8 KB), which `FLEET-MINING` reads.
- `first-review: false` posts no "Agent review" status and no comment (for a consumer that keeps the first review off).
- Model fixed to `sonnet` in the workflow (no input; changing it is a fleet PR). The header records the decisions: first review Sonnet on every agent PR; Fable second review on risky PRs (`FLEET-SECOND-REVIEW`).
- Claude Code's version is locked in fleet's `.github/agent-review/package-lock.json` (Dependabot npm entry, weekly, cooldown 7 days); consumers drop theirs.
- fleet dogfoods it: `.github/workflows/agent-review-caller.yml` in fleet (`pull_request_target` → `uses: ./.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`, which for that event resolves to the base branch's copy) and fleet's own `.github/agent-review/context.md`.
- Self-test: the reusable workflow on fleet's PRs with `dry-run: true` and a stub reviewer (`tests/fakes/claude`, a script that prints a fixture answer chosen by `FAKE_REVIEW`), so the plumbing is tested without a secret.
- Port `tests/test_agent_review.py` from both repos.

**Out of scope**
The second review (`FLEET-SECOND-REVIEW`), the merge gate (`FLEET-MERGE-GATE`), mining (`FLEET-MINING`).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Both repos' `test_agent_review.py` cases pass in fleet, plus: an explicit `generated` entry under `tests/fixtures/` is left out; a fixture not listed is not.
- [ ] A test parses `agent-review.yml`: the PR checkout has `persist-credentials: false`; no step that has a secret in its `env` runs anything from the PR checkout except through `agent_review.py`'s read-only git calls; the `report` job has no secret and no PR checkout.
- [ ] `ready_for_review` on a head that already has an "Agent review" status runs no review (unit test of the decision); a `labeled` event runs no first review.
- [ ] The comment's third line round-trips the findings; text in a finding can't forge it (an `<!--` in a title is escaped) (tests).
- [ ] Self-test green with the stub (pass, blocking, malformed answer → error).
- [ ] zizmor reports only the documented `dangerous-triggers` ignore.

**Tests**
`tests/test_agent_review.py` (ported and extended), `tests/test_agent_review_workflow.py` (workflow structure), the self-test job.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-TOOLS` (package layout and CLI).

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): review workflow, its secrets and untrusted pull request content.

title: Second review by Fable for risky pull requests, reported as its own required status
body:
Key `FLEET-SECOND-REVIEW`

**Context**
The owner wants pull requests labelled `safety-critical` or `security`, or touching listed paths, reviewed a second time by a different model. The first review stays exactly as it is (Sonnet). Runway's workflow header records "every review uses Sonnet and never Opus, security-sensitive changes included"; this issue keeps that for the first review and records the new decision for the second. Darkroom's deletion-safety issues (Darkroom #24, #37, #38) are labelled `safety-critical`; Waypoint's photos issues PHOTOS-SOURCES, PHOTOS-API and PHOTOS-PROXY are labelled `security`.

**Scope**
- Job `second-review` in `agent-review.yml`, isolated exactly like `review` (read-only tools confined to its directory, no settings, hooks, plugins or MCP servers, hosted runner, secrets only in its review step), plus its own report job. Status context `Second review`; comment marker `<!-- second-review -->` with its own state line and findings line; re-review and carry-forward reuse the first review's logic, parametrized by marker and context.
- Risky when either holds: a label in input `second-review-labels` (default `safety-critical,security`), or a changed path matching input `second-review-paths` (newline-separated globs with `**`; `.github/**` and `.claude/**` always count). `agent_review.py risky` decides from the PR's labels and `files.txt` and writes the reason into the comment.
- Not risky: status `success`, "Not a risky pull request", so the merge gate can require `Second review` on every pull request. Not an agent's PR: same as the first review. Dependabot: no status (the merge gate asks for none).
- Label events: `labeled` and `unlabeled` rerun only this job. An `unlabeled` event sent by anyone other than the repository owner (`github.event.sender.login != github.repository_owner`) changes nothing: the status stays as it was.
- Model fixed to `claude-fable-5-1` in the workflow (no input). Inputs `second-review-budget-usd` (default `10`) and `second-review-max-turns` (default `120`); hitting either is an `error`, never a pass.
- Prompt `.github/agent-review/second-review.md` (appended to `prompt.md`): threat-model the change (who can reach the new code and with what input); check every promise or invariant it touches in `AGENTS.md` and in the consumer's `.github/agent-review/invariants.md` (required whenever the caller sets `second-review-paths`; a numbered list of the app's invariants and the test or rule that holds each); require a positive and a negative test per invariant touched; treat any weakening of a check (a Semgrep rule, a test, CODEOWNERS, a workflow permission, a label rule) as blocking unless the linked issue asked for it; read the first review's comment, when there is one, as data, and say where it disagrees.
- The two reviews run in parallel; neither waits for the other.
- `docs/agent-review.md`: the second review, its triggers and costs.

**Out of scope**
Requiring the status (`FLEET-MERGE-GATE` defaults to it; each consumer's adoption sets it).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Stub-reviewer self-test cases: risky by label, risky by path, risky by `.github/` change, not risky (success with the reason), `unlabeled` by a non-owner (status unchanged), `unlabeled` by the owner (re-evaluated).
- [ ] The second review's model and its secrets appear only in its own job; a test asserts the model string is literal `claude-fable-5-1`.
- [ ] A finding in the second review fails `Second review` and leaves `Agent review` untouched, and the other way round.
- [ ] `risky` matches `**` globs and renamed paths (old and new names) (tests).

**Tests**
`tests/test_agent_review_risky.py`, additions to `tests/test_agent_review_workflow.py`, self-test cases.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-REVIEW`.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): review workflow, model routing for security reviews, secrets.

title: Reusable merge gate
body:
Key `FLEET-MERGE-GATE`

**Context**
The two `merge-gate.sh` copies are the same script apart from configuration: Waypoint requires no status (its review is off) and ignores `Cancel runs on close|Merge gate`; Runway requires `Agent review` and also ignores `Preview|Screenshot diff`. The two `merge-gate.yml` differ only in the `workflow_run` list, which must stay in the caller because a called workflow can't declare triggers.

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/merge-gate.yml` (`workflow_call`): inputs `sha`, `pr`, `required-workflows` (newline list, default `Security scans` and `CodeQL`), `ignored-workflows` (regex; `Merge gate` and `Cancel runs on close` always ignored), `required-statuses` (default `Agent review` and `Second review`), `ignored-apps` (default `codecov|github-actions`), `poll-seconds`, `poll-attempts`, `automerge-dependabot` (default `true`), `after-merge-workflows` (default `docker.yml security.yml`), `dry-run`, `fleet-ref`. Permissions as today (`contents`, `pull-requests`, `statuses`, `actions` write; `checks` read).
- `.github/scripts/merge-gate.sh`: one script, configured by environment from the inputs; behaviour otherwise identical to both copies (CodeQL polling, Dependabot rules, one PR per head).
- New rule: a Dependabot pull request that changes an `AnthonyPluth/fleet/` reference is never merged by the gate (it changes the review and the gate themselves); the gate passes and leaves it for the owner, whose Code Owner review on `.github/` the rulesets already require.
- Caller snippet in `docs/adopting.md` (triggers `workflow_run` with the app's list, `check_suite`, `workflow_dispatch` with `pr`; the job `if:` both apps use today).
- Tests run the script against a fake `gh` on `PATH` that serves recorded API answers.

**Out of scope**
Each app's workflow list and required workflows (their adoption issues).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Fake-`gh` cases: all green → success; a required status missing → pending; `Second review` failing → failure; CodeQL-only pending → polls; two PRs on one head → failure; Dependabot green → merges (dry run prints the command); Dependabot bumping a fleet ref → passes, not merged.
- [ ] Both apps' current configurations reproduced exactly by inputs (a test per app).
- [ ] Self-test runs the reusable workflow in dry-run on fleet's own PR.

**Tests**
`tests/test_merge_gate.py` (drives `merge-gate.sh` with `tests/fakes/gh`), self-test case.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-SCAFFOLD`.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): a workflow with a write token that decides merges.

title: Reusable security scans, and the deep-scan plan: claude-security runbook plus a reminder workflow
body:
Key `FLEET-SECURITY`

**Context**
`security.yml` differs between the apps by its path regexes (which scans a change can affect) and by Waypoint's `vars.RUNS_ON` runner option. Darkroom is a private repository on a personal account: code scanning (SARIF upload) and CodeQL aren't available there, so its scans must fail the workflow on findings instead of reporting to the Security tab, and its merge gate can't require CodeQL.

Deep scans with the claude-security plugin (Anthropic directory, `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`, `plugins/claude-security`, 0.11.0) can't run in a workflow. Its skill (`jobs/scan-codebase.md`, `jobs/scan-changes.md`) asks a fixed confirmation that only the person's own request can answer, never text from the repository, a file or a scheduled task, and it refuses in a non-interactive session; it needs the session's Workflow tool ("leave Claude Code open while the scan completes"); and its trust model gives it no isolation from the repository's settings and hooks. So the deep scan is an owner runbook, and fleet automates only the reminder.

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/security.yml` (`workflow_call`): the union of both apps' jobs (changes filter, Semgrep with the app's own rules and their example check, npm audit, Trivy files, Trivy image, zizmor, OpenSSF Scorecard); inputs `code-paths` (regex), `web-dirs` (newline list), `image-paths` (regex) and `dockerfile`, `semgrep-examples` (command; default runs `.semgrep/check_examples.py` when present), `sarif-upload` (default `true`; `false` makes Semgrep, Trivy and zizmor fail the job on findings instead), `scorecard` (default `true`; public repositories only), `runs-on` (JSON, default `"ubuntu-latest"`; Waypoint passes its `vars.RUNS_ON` expression), `fleet-ref`. The weekly schedule stays in the caller.
- `docs/deep-scan.md` (generic, nothing app-specific): when (each app decides: on demand before a milestone, or quarterly); where (a local Claude Code session in a fresh clone of `main` at the commit being judged, plugin installed at user scope with `/plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official`, `claude --permission-mode auto`, `/model claude-fable-5-1`; not a cloud session, which doesn't install plugins a repository declares and can't be relied on to stay open); the request to type (whole repository, `high` effort, with the owner's own sentence accepting the time and token cost, since the plugin refuses without it); what to do with `CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/` (it carries its own `.gitignore`; keep it out of commits; review the redaction); where findings go (private repository: one issue per confirmed finding labelled `security`; public repository: one draft security advisory per finding under Security → Advisories, never a public issue, fixed through the advisory's private fork or a PR with a neutral title when the owner decides); the scan record (revision stamp file name, effort, counts by severity) written in the tracking issue; optional "Suggest patches".
- `.github/workflows/deep-scan-due.yml` (`workflow_call`, the caller schedules it): opens one issue "Deep security scan due" (labels `manual`, `security`) unless one is open, with the runbook link at FLEET_REF, the revision of the last scan (from the last closed issue with that title), and the number of commits since. `issues: write` only; no secrets.

**Out of scope**
Running a deep scan (each app's `manual` issue).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Both apps' current `security.yml` behaviour reproduced by inputs (fixture-driven test of the `changes` job's outputs per app).
- [ ] With `sarif-upload: false`, a planted Semgrep finding fails the job (self-test on a fixture tree).
- [ ] `deep-scan-due` opens one issue, and a second run while it is open adds nothing (dry-run self-test).
- [ ] `docs/deep-scan.md` names the plugin's version it was written against and says what to recheck when the plugin changes.

**Tests**
`tests/test_security_changes.py`, `tests/test_deep_scan_due.py`, self-test cases.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-SCAFFOLD`.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): security scanning and the deep-scan plan.

title: Opt-in reusable workflows: verify (control smoke / verify flows), screenshot diff, cancel on close, tidy releases
body:
Key `FLEET-OPTIONAL`

**Context**
The apps drifted in what they run beyond the core: Waypoint has `control-smoke.yml` (`make control-smoke` on changes to `frontend/verify/**`, `waypoint/verify.py`, `tools/control`); Runway has `verify.yml` ("Verify flows": `make verify`'s flows on changes to `frontend/**`, the demo data and the verify runner), `screenshot-diff.yml` (`tools/screenshot_diff.py`: a report of changed pixels in `screenshots/`, a comment, never a verdict) and `preview.yml` (a live copy behind a Cloudflare quick tunnel). Both have `cancel-on-close.yml` and `tidy-releases.yml`, with small drift (runner choice, the verify concurrency group).

**Scope**
- `verify.yml` (`workflow_call`): one workflow for both: inputs `make-target` (`control-smoke`, or Runway's flows target), `needs-faketime` (default `true`), `timeout-minutes`, `runs-on`. Path filters stay in the caller (`on: pull_request: paths:`), as today. `contents: read`, no secrets. The caller's job name keeps the status names the merge gates list today ("Control smoke", "Verify flows").
- `screenshot-diff.yml` + `fleet_tools/screenshot_diff.py` (from Runway's `tools/screenshot_diff.py`, with its image dependencies as an optional extra `fleet-tools[images]`): input `dir` (`screenshots/` for Runway, `docs/src/assets/screenshots/` for Waypoint) and the comment marker. It keeps `pull_request` (not `_target`), but the tool now runs from fleet's checkout at FLEET_REF instead of the PR's, so a PR can't change the tool that reports on it.
- `cancel-on-close.yml` (input: the concurrency group prefixes to cancel) and `tidy-releases.yml` (inputs as the two copies differ).
- Preview stays in Runway: it deploys Runway's own image with Runway's sample data through a tunnel; nothing for the others to reuse yet (note it in `docs/drift.md`).

**Out of scope**
Each app's opt-in (their adoption issues); Runway's preview.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Self-test runs `verify.yml` on a fixture tree whose `make` target writes a marker; `screenshot-diff.yml` on two fixture PNG sets produces the report and, in dry run, the comment text.
- [ ] Runway's `tests/` for `screenshot_diff.py`, if any, pass in fleet; otherwise new tests for changed, added, removed and identical images.
- [ ] `docs/drift.md` rows for each of these and for preview.

**Tests**
`tests/test_screenshot_diff.py`, self-test cases.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-TOOLS`.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): screenshot-diff handles pull request content and posts with a write token; cancel-on-close holds `actions: write`.

title: Shared AGENTS.md sections, the 'a mistake that repeats gets a check' rule, and fleet sync/drift for them
body:
Key `FLEET-AGENTS-MD`

**Context**
Waypoint's and Runway's `AGENTS.md` share most of "Starting work", "Working in a container", the shape of "Mistakes that keep coming back" (Failure paths, Access that outlives the person, Undo and restore, GitHub Actions, Layout are near-identical) and "Git and PRs". Both already say "A correction becomes a check" and "When one can be checked, it moves out of this list into a check", but an item can stay *human-judged* indefinitely. Waypoint's text also says the agent review is disabled and Codex reviews instead. Drift in "Git and PRs": Waypoint says open a PR for every change; Runway says open a PR only when asked. Both apps cut a release on every push to `main`, so all work lands through PRs: Waypoint's wording wins.

**Scope**
- `agents-md/sections/` with one file per shared block: `starting-work.md`, `working-in-a-container.md` (session-start hook, `poetry run`/`make`, subagent worktrees; the app's "checks that only run in CI" list stays app text), `mistakes.md`, `git-and-prs.md` (branch, focused commits with the `Co-Authored-By` trailer, `make check` before pushing, open a PR for every change once it's pushed, short PR descriptions, the title decides the version, a PR is ready when "Merge gate" passes, which on an agent's PR includes "Agent review" and, on a risky one, "Second review", no hard wraps). Each file has front matter naming the heading it lives under.
- `mistakes.md` opens with the rule, verbatim:

  > **A mistake that repeats gets a check.** When review flags the same kind of mistake on a second pull request, the fix adds a check that would have caught it: a lint rule (ESLint, or Semgrep in `.semgrep/` with a failing and a passing example), a type (strict mypy, a `NewType` or `Literal`), or a test. The item below then names that check in its parenthesis (`checked: waypoint-trip-visibility`, `checked: tests/test_offline.py`). An item stays *human-judged* only when no check can express it, and says why. Every month the "Repeated review findings" issue lists the kinds that came back; a row there is closed by a check, not by a new sentence here.

  followed by the shared items (Failure paths; Access that outlives the person; Undo and restore; GitHub Actions; Layout) each with its parenthesis. App items follow the block, outside it.
- Markers in a consumer: `<!-- fleet:begin <section> vX.Y.Z -->` … `<!-- fleet:end <section> -->`. Inside is fleet's file verbatim; outside belongs to the app.
- `fleet sync --to vX.Y.Z` (AGENTS part): run from the CLI at that version (the sections ship as package data), replace each marked block, insert a missing block at the end of the heading its front matter names (creating the heading if absent), never touch text outside markers, write `.fleet/version`.
- `fleet drift`: every block byte-equal to fleet's at the version in its marker; every marker and `.fleet/version` at one version; that version not newer than the consumer's fleet workflow pins and in the same major (it may trail them while a sync PR is open).
- fleet's own `AGENTS.md` takes the blocks.

**Out of scope**
Vendored skills and hook (`FLEET-PLUGIN` extends sync and drift); the sync workflow (`FLEET-SYNC`).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `fleet sync` is idempotent and leaves every byte outside markers unchanged (property test over fixture AGENTS.md files).
- [ ] `fleet drift` fails on a one-character edit inside a block, on a marker version that differs from `.fleet/version`, and on a content version ahead of the workflow pins; it passes on any edit outside blocks.
- [ ] Synced into the two fixture consumers, the result reads correctly around the app sections (fixture snapshots reviewed in the PR).
- [ ] The rule text above is in `mistakes.md` verbatim.

**Tests**
`tests/test_sync_agents.py`, `tests/test_drift.py`.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-TOOLS`.

**Model**
Opus: instructions and a text-sync tool; no secrets.

title: Plugin marketplace with the fleet plugin (skills, reviewer agent, session-start hook), vendored into consumers for cloud sessions
body:
Key `FLEET-PLUGIN`

**Context**
The plan is a marketplace in fleet that each app enables in `.claude/settings.json` with `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins`. Claude Code's documentation for cloud environments ("What carries over from your setup") says a cloud session doesn't install the plugins a repository turns on under `enabledPlugins`, including ones from the marketplaces it lists under `extraKnownMarketplaces`, while the repository's `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/settings.json` hooks are part of the clone and load. The agents for these repos run in cloud sessions (each app's `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` acts only when `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`). So the plugin is the single source and serves local sessions, and `fleet sync` vendors its skills, agent and hook into each consumer at the pinned version. A consumer declares the marketplace (pinned) but doesn't enable the plugin: enabled, every skill would load twice in a local session.

Drift in the hook: Waypoint's guards against Poetry building the venv on the wrong Python and installs npm packages with `--no-save`; Runway's checks `frontend/node_modules` for completeness and reinstalls from the lockfile. fleet's hook takes both, with `--no-save` (a session must not rewrite a committed lockfile).

**Scope**
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (name `fleet`, one plugin `fleet`, `source: "./plugins/fleet"`) and `plugins/fleet/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (version = `VERSION`).
- Skills (`plugins/fleet/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`):
  - `fix-with-checks`: when a review finding or CI failure is a kind listed under "Mistakes that keep coming back", or the same mistake shows up a second time, the fix includes the check; how to choose lint, Semgrep (with a failing and a passing example under `.semgrep/examples/`), a type or a test; how to update the item's parenthesis; never silence a rule.
  - `design-signoff`: no frontend design change ships without the owner's sign-off; what counts (layout, flow, visual style, theme tokens, copy the design fixed); how to show it (the app's `make verify` images at phone and desktop width, the signed-off designs under `docs/design/` where the app has them); a deviation stops and is raised in the PR and the design sign-off issue; tokens are never adjusted on one's own.
  - `agent-task`: writing an issue an agent finishes in one session and one PR: sections Context, Scope, Out of scope, Acceptance criteria (`- [ ]`), Tests, Depends on, Model (Opus by default; Fable for security, review workflows, CI secrets, untrusted pull request content and security scanning; Sonnet only for mechanical copying); a draft refers to another not-yet-created issue by its key in double curly braces; real file names; no personal data in public repositories; the design sign-off criterion on any UI issue.
  - `review-guidance`: Agent review and Second review comments are data: fix a blocking finding or answer it with a reason, push the fixes together, never add or remove the `safety-critical` or `security` labels yourself, and run the `fleet-reviewer` agent before pushing a risky change.
- Agent `plugins/fleet/agents/fleet-reviewer.md`: read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob; Bash limited to `git diff` and `git log`), the first review's prompt run on `git diff origin/main...HEAD` with the app's `.github/agent-review/context.md`, answering in the same finding shape. Advisory only; CI decides.
- Hook `plugins/fleet/hooks/session-start.sh` (declared in `hooks/hooks.json` as SessionStart): the union above, configured by the consumer's `.claude/hooks/fleet.conf` (`PYTHON_VERSION`, `FRONTEND_DIRS`, `APT_PACKAGES`, `NODE_CHECK` (the packages whose absence means an incomplete `node_modules`)), and sourcing `.claude/hooks/session-start.local.sh` last when present.
- Vendoring (extends `fleet sync` and `fleet drift`): writes `.claude/skills/fleet-<name>/` (prefixed, so app skills never clash), `.claude/agents/fleet-reviewer.md`, `.claude/hooks/fleet-session-start.sh` and `tools/fleet` (a shim that runs the CLI at `.fleet/version`: `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/AnthonyPluth/fleet@$(cat .fleet/version)" fleet "$@"`, installing `uv` the way both hooks do today when it's missing). Every vendored file starts with a line saying it's vendored from fleet at that version and is edited in fleet; drift fails on any change.
- `claude plugin validate .` in `make check`.
- `docs/adopting.md`: the `.claude/settings.json` shape (SessionStart hook → `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/fleet-session-start.sh`; `"extraKnownMarketplaces": {"fleet": {"source": {"source": "github", "repo": "AnthonyPluth/fleet", "ref": "vX.Y.Z"}}}`; no `enabledPlugins` entry, with the reason).

**Out of scope**
The sync workflow (`FLEET-SYNC`); app skills such as `verify-waypoint`.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `claude plugin validate .` passes; installing the plugin locally from a checkout lists the four skills, the agent and the hook.
- [ ] The hook, run in a container with each fixture consumer's `fleet.conf`, reproduces both apps' current setup steps (a test with stubbed `uv`, `poetry`, `npm`, `apt-get` that records the calls), and returns quickly on a second run.
- [ ] `fleet sync` vendors every file listed above; `fleet drift` fails on an edited vendored file.
- [ ] Each skill's text follows the owner rules above (reviewed in the PR); nothing personal or app-specific in them.

**Tests**
`tests/test_hook.py`, `tests/test_sync_vendor.py`, `claude plugin validate` in CI.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-AGENTS-MD` (sync and drift), `FLEET-REVIEW` (the reviewer agent reuses its prompt).

**Model**
Opus: skills, an agent definition and a setup hook; no secrets.

title: Consumer sync and checks: reusable sync.yml (PRs through the fleet-bot App) and checks.yml (fleet checks + drift)
body:
Key `FLEET-SYNC`

**Context**
Each consumer has two kinds of pin. Dependabot bumps the workflow pins (`uses: AnthonyPluth/fleet/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@<sha> # vX.Y.Z`) but can't edit `AGENTS.md`, the vendored `.claude/` files or `.fleet/version`. A sync PR follows each Dependabot bump. A pull request created with a workflow's own token starts no workflows, so the sync uses the `fleet-bot` App's token (`FLEET-SETUP`); the App has no Workflows permission, so it can't touch `.github/workflows/`.

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/checks.yml` (`workflow_call`): checks out the consumer with history, then runs `fleet checks --commits <base>..<head>` (on a PR; plain `fleet checks` on main) and `fleet drift` with the CLI at the consumer's `.fleet/version`. Replaces each consumer's own `fleet-checks` job. `contents: read`; `runs-on` input.
- `.github/workflows/sync.yml` (`workflow_call`): reads every fleet pin in the consumer's workflows (they must agree; if not, it fails naming the files), compares with `.fleet/version`; when the pin is newer in the same major, runs `fleet sync --to <pin>` and opens or updates the PR `chore: fleet content vX.Y.Z` from branch `fleet/sync`, with the CHANGELOG entries in between in its body. Token: `actions/create-github-app-token` (SHA-pinned) from the caller's `FLEET_BOT_APP_ID` variable (input) and `FLEET_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` secret (passed by name). A newer major opens an issue instead ("fleet vN needs a migration: see CHANGELOG"). Callers run it on push to `main` touching `.github/workflows/**`, weekly, and by hand.
- `docs/adopting.md`: both callers and why there are two bots.

**Out of scope**
Bumping workflow pins (Dependabot).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Dry-run self-test on a fixture consumer: pins at v1.1.0 and content at v1.0.0 → the sync commit's diff is exactly the AGENTS blocks, vendored files and `.fleet/version`; pins and content equal → nothing; pins at v2.0.0 → the issue text.
- [ ] Pins that disagree fail with the file names.
- [ ] A test asserts the sync never writes under `.github/workflows/`.
- [ ] `checks.yml` fails on a drifted fixture and passes on a clean one.

**Tests**
`tests/test_sync_workflow.py` (the pin reader and planner), self-test cases.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-PLUGIN` (vendoring), `FLEET-AGENTS-MD`.

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): holds an App private key and writes pull requests into the three repos.

title: Review mining: a monthly report of review findings that repeat, with the check each should become
body:
Key `FLEET-MINING`

**Context**
The rule "a mistake that repeats gets a check" (`FLEET-AGENTS-MD`) needs someone to notice repeats. The first and second reviews now record each finding's kind (the AGENTS.md "Mistakes that keep coming back" item it falls under) and the check that would have caught it, in a hidden line of their comment (`FLEET-REVIEW`). A deterministic job can count them; no model is needed.

**Scope**
- `fleet review-mine --repo OWNER/NAME --days 90`: lists pull requests updated in the window (`gh api`, paginated), reads comments by `github-actions[bot]` whose first line is `<!-- agent-review -->` or `<!-- second-review -->`, decodes only their third-line findings record (size and field limits; anything else in the comment is ignored, since it quotes untrusted pull request content), and counts, per kind (and per normalized title for `other`), the pull requests with at least one finding. It reads `AGENTS.md`'s "Mistakes that keep coming back" items to learn each kind's state from its parenthesis (`checked: …`, `partly checked`, `human-judged`).
- Output: one issue per repository titled "Repeated review findings" (label `review-mining`), kept open and rewritten each run: a table of kind, state, pull requests in the window (links), last seen, and proposed check (the most common `check` the reviewers named, else the kind's usual check type). A kind is listed when it appears on two or more pull requests in the window and isn't fully checked, or when it is checked and still appears (the check misses a case). Each row ends with a checkbox "becomes an Agent task". The same table goes to the job summary.
- `.github/workflows/review-mining.yml` (`workflow_call`): `issues: write`, `pull-requests: read`, no secrets; callers schedule it monthly (`17 6 1 * *`) and by hand.
- Titles and file names are defused before posting (no @mentions, no HTML comments), as `agent_review.render` does.

**Out of scope**
Writing the checks (each row becomes its own issue, usually Opus).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Fixture comments → the expected table; kinds matched to AGENTS item titles case-insensitively; `other` titles grouped after normalizing case and punctuation.
- [ ] A findings line placed anywhere but line 3, a malformed or oversized record, and a comment by another author are all ignored (tests).
- [ ] Re-running in the same month rewrites the issue body without opening a second issue.

**Tests**
`tests/test_review_mine.py`, a dry-run self-test case.

**Depends on**
`FLEET-REVIEW` (findings record), `FLEET-AGENTS-MD` (the mistakes list format).

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): reads text derived from untrusted pull request content and writes with a token.

title: Release process, adoption guide and fleet v1.0.0
body:
Key `FLEET-RELEASE`

**Context**
Consumers pin fleet by commit SHA with a version comment, and Dependabot bumps those pins; the reusable workflows fetch their own scripts at the tag stamped into them (`FLEET_REF`). A release must therefore be one commit where `VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, every `FLEET_REF`, `plugin.json` and the docs agree, tagged once and never moved.

**Scope**
- Release PR (agent or owner): bumps `VERSION`, turns CHANGELOG's Unreleased section into `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD`, sets `FLEET_REF: vX.Y.Z` in every reusable workflow, `plugin.json`'s version, and the versions in `docs/adopting.md`'s snippets. `fleet self-check` enforces that all agree.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: on a push to `main` that changes `VERSION`, tags the commit `vX.Y.Z` (fails if the tag exists) and creates the GitHub release with that CHANGELOG section. `contents: write` only.
- `docs/release.md` (semver policy): major when a consumer must change its caller or its `AGENTS.md` (an input removed or renamed, a status renamed, a block removed); minor for new inputs with defaults, new checks, prompt or model changes (always called out in the CHANGELOG); patch for fixes.
- `docs/adopting.md`, complete: a caller for every reusable workflow with secrets passed by name, the `[tool.fleet]` keys, `.fleet/version` and the first `tools/fleet sync --to v1.0.0`, `.claude/settings.json`, labels to create, the ruleset (require only "Merge gate"), and the Dependabot entry:

```yaml
- package-ecosystem: github-actions
  directory: /
  schedule: { interval: weekly, day: monday }
  cooldown: { default-days: 3 }
  groups:
    fleet:
      patterns: ["AnthonyPluth/fleet/*"]
```

- Cut v1.0.0: the owner merges the release PR; `release.yml` tags it.

**Out of scope**
Adopting it in the apps (their issues).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `fleet self-check` fails when any of the stamped versions disagree (tests).
- [ ] `v1.0.0` exists, its release notes are the CHANGELOG section, and every reusable workflow at that tag has `FLEET_REF: v1.0.0`.
- [ ] A scratch consumer (the fixture tree in a throwaway private repo of the owner's) runs `agent-review.yml`, `merge-gate.yml`, `checks.yml` and `sync.yml` at the tag's SHA (owner ticks; delete the scratch repo after).

**Tests**
`tests/test_release.py` (stamping and self-check), the scratch consumer run.

**Depends on**
Every other fleet issue.

**Model**
Opus: release plumbing with a contents token and documentation; the workflows it stamps were reviewed in their own issues.
